claims.text: The target materials are multicomponent high-entropy alloys containing at least five elements.
The target alloys can have ordered or disordered solid states.
The target alloys have liquid states accessible at or near their high melting temperatures.
Replacing an EAM reference with an in situ machine-learning potential trained on solid and liquid ab initio configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Neural-network or Gaussian-approximation potentials can be trained on a broad range of solid and highly disordered liquid ab initio configurations for the target HEAs.
The proposed method is applicable at approximately 0.8–1.0 times the alloy melting temperature.
High-temperature HEA liquids exhibit many accessible atomic configurations.
Traditional EAM training sets can fail to represent sufficient configurational diversity in the ab initio liquid.
The greater flexibility of the machine-learning potential will better reproduce local energetics and diverse coordination environments in the ab initio liquid.
Better reproduction of liquid coordination environments will enhance sampling of relevant atomic configurations.
The machine-learning reference will lower the energetic difference between the reference and the ab initio target.
Lowering the reference–target energetic difference will increase statistical overlap along the thermodynamic-integration path.
The machine-learning reference will provide a smoother connection between the reference and ab initio free-energy landscapes.
Relative to TOR-TILD EAM references, the intervention will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by an estimated 40–60%.
Reduced path mismatch will produce more accurate solid- and liquid-state free-energy calculations.
The improvement will be less pronounced for alloys with lower compositional complexity.
Incomplete coverage of relevant configuration space by the training database will reduce the benefit of the machine-learning reference.
The magnitude of improvement depends on the quality and extent of the ab initio training data.

The hypothesis is falsified if the machine-learning reference yields less than a 30% improvement in path mismatch or produces free energies outside uncertainty bounds relative to ab initio benchmarks.
